_comment: Fragment 31 — D-75, development build lanes. Three Lines applied to the build, not the product. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-75 — Development Build Lanes (A/B/C)
nodes.description: Binding assignment of the three development agents to lettered lanes in a fixed phase order. Lane A is Claude Code (docs, register, specs) in Phase 1; Lane B is Codex (app, lib, migrations 0002+) in Phase 2; Lane C is Antigravity (workflows, checks, gitattributes, deploy gate) in Phase 3. Work outside the active lane is specified, never applied. Crossing a lane boundary requires a handoff, not a commit.
nodes.rationale: The phase order existed only in the Chief Editor's intent. A grep for orchestrat, role, phase and lane across all four agent rule and workflow files returned zero hits, and the register assigned no agent a role, so an agent that orchestrated and built and touched CI was complying with the build rules rather than disobeying them.

nodes.label: Lanes Are Lettered So They Cannot Be Confused With the Product's Lines
nodes.description: Development lanes are lettered A, B and C. The product's Three Lines are numbered 1, 2 and 3 and are carried by line_assignment, AC-01, AC-05 and AC-17 under OD1 to OD3. Both derive from the same IIA source principle that forbids merging roles, but they govern different subjects and must not be cross-referenced. OD4, Proposer to Critics to Judge, is separate again.
nodes.rationale: Reusing the numbers would have created one term with two referents in a corpus that cross-references constantly. That is the defect found in D-73's digital twin, where an established phrase meaning virtual agents serving one natural person was reused to mean a multi-tenant product, and the trap warned about at D-31 and D-33.

nodes.label: Three Lane Crossings in Four Commits
nodes.description: Commits 24b39fb through 833f52b decided Q10, which is the Chief Editor's call, wrote scripts/checks/docs-drift.mjs, which is Lane C, and committed .gitattributes, which is also Lane C. None was recorded as a crossing. The docs-drift check produced that way cannot fail: nothing writes .graphify/needs_update and it reports PASS synced against a modified document.
nodes.rationale: Recorded as evidence that the defect is live rather than theoretical. Lane A's own analysis crossed the same boundary twice on the same day, troubleshooting a pipeline belonging to Lane C and judging Phase 1 against Phase 3 deployment criteria, and both were withdrawn.

nodes.label: main Lagging the Working Branch Is Expected Until Phase 3
nodes.description: Deployment belongs to Lane C and to GitHub. No agent deploys. The working branch standing many commits ahead of main during Phase 1 is the correct state for a specs-only phase and is explicitly not a defect to report.
nodes.rationale: Written down because Lane A reported it as a defect once already. Judging a phase against criteria that do not yet apply is a measurement detached from its subject, the same family as the probe that cannot fail.
